escalation.reason: measured FPR 1.0 > sealed bar 0.3 (Art. L: the attacker is measured non-selective; its KILL is inadmissible as a terminal verdict and is escalated with the objection preserved)
escalation.rule: the instrument's KILL is measured non-selective (FPR above the sealed bar); the objection is preserved verbatim and ESCALATED for adjudication — the candidate is NOT killed by this attack alone (Art. L); the deterministic gates are unchanged

preserved_objections.basis: The proposed debiasing algorithm fundamentally misunderstands feedback loop dynamics in collaborative filtering systems. The intervention of periodically resetting training data with random cold-start samples introduces more noise than signal, as demonstrated by the evidence in [doi:10.1145/3308560.3317303] which shows that random sampling degrades recommendation quality rather than improving diversity.

The candidate fails to specify critical boundary conditions such as system scale (number of users/items), computational constraints, or the ratio of cold-start to existing data. Without these parameters, the intervention cannot be properly evaluated or implemented, making it fundamentally unusable in production environments as noted in [doi:10.3850/978-981-07-3043-7_090].

The evidence bundle contains irrelevant citations including GNSS trajectory analysis [doi:10.1109/icecet65726.2026.11632531], tourism sentiment analysis [doi:10.31004/riggs.v4i4.4373], and banking data mining [doi:10.3390/bdcc2030018], which contradict the claimed domain expertise and demonstrate a fundamental misunderstanding of recommender systems literature.

The predicted effect of maintaining recommendation diversity while preserving long-term engagement directly contradicts the baseline evidence showing that collaborative filtering systems naturally optimize for short-term engagement at the expense of diversity, as demonstrated in [doi:10.1145/3308560.3317303]. The candidate fails to explain how their intervention would overcome this fundamental limitation without degrading overall performance.

The proposed intervention requires identifying "cold-start user interactions" which is computationally infeasible in large-scale systems, as it would necessitate real-time classification of user interaction patterns while maintaining high request throughput. This violates the fundamental scalability requirements of modern recommendation systems as described in [doi:10.3850/978-981-07-3043-7_090].

The testable prediction focuses solely on retention rates without defining how to isolate the effect of the debiasing algorithm from other retention factors. Without controlling for content quality changes, marketing campaigns, or seasonal effects, the measurement is fundamentally ambiguous and cannot validly test the hypothesis, rendering the prediction meaningless.
